title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 10 Mathematics · Chapter 4 Quadratic Equations (NCERT reprint 2026-27)
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions modelled on question types that have repeated in CBSE board papers 2022-2026 and the Sample Question Papers 2024-25 to 2026-27. They are practice for readiness, not predictions of what will appear in any exam.
instructions: 40 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number (negative allowed). No calculator.

patterns.P2: Find k for equal (or real) roots

S1.name: Standard form: is it a quadratic equation?
S1.tip: Write it as ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0, but simplify first: x² terms can cancel (linear) and x³ terms can cancel (quadratic).

S2.name: Roots by factorisation (and a given root)
S2.tip: Split the middle term into two parts whose product is ac, factorise, set each factor to 0. A given root makes the equation true: substitute it.

S3.name: Surd and repeated roots
S3.tip: With surds, ac may still be a whole number (√2 × 5√2 = 10). A perfect square (px − q)² gives two equal roots q/p.

S4.name: Quadratic formula and nature of roots
S4.tip: D = b² − 4ac: D > 0 two distinct real roots, D = 0 two equal roots (−b/2a), D < 0 no real roots. Formula x = (−b ± √D)/2a.

S5.name: Find k for equal or real roots
S5.tip: Equal roots: set D = 0. Expand brackets first, keep both signs of k, and reject a k that makes a = 0. Real roots: D ≥ 0.

S6.name: Word problems: numbers, digits, ages
S6.tip: Numbers: x(S − x) = P. Reciprocals: 1/x + 1/y = (x + y)/xy. Digits 10t + u. Ages: add the same years to both. Reject impossible roots.

S7.name: Word problems: speed and time
S7.tip: time = distance ÷ speed. 'Takes 30 min less' → old time − new time = 1/2. Upstream speed − stream, downstream speed + stream.
S7.ncert: NCERT Exercise 4.1 Q2(iv) type; past-paper 5-mark type

S8.name: Is it possible? Geometry problems
S8.tip: 'Is it possible?' Form the equation, then check D (D < 0 → not possible). Right triangles: Pythagoras, then reject the negative root.

S9.name: Case study: area with a uniform strip
S9.tip: Strip of width x outside an a × b rectangle: (a + 2x)(b + 2x); inside: (a − 2x)(b − 2x). Reject a width that makes a side negative.

questions.question: Two numbers have sum 25 and product 156. Find the larger number.
The sum of the squares of two consecutive positive integers is 181. Find the larger integer.
questions.explanation: x² + (x + 1)² = 181 → x² + x − 90 = 0 → x = 9; the integers are 9 and 10.

questions.question: The product of the digits of a two-digit number is 18. When 27 is subtracted from the number, the digits interchange. Find the number.
questions.explanation: Tens t, units u: tu = 18 and (10t + u) − 27 = 10u + t → t − u = 3. t(t − 3) = 18 → t = 6, u = 3. Check: 63 − 27 = 36.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: digits are 0-9, reject negatives.
